# PersonPicture

Header: `winui/ui/media/PersonPicture.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/PersonPicture.hpp`.

A circular avatar showing a photo, initials or a placeholder glyph, with an optional badge. It takes no input and never receives focus.

What it shows, in priority order:
- the "People" glyph when [`is_group()`](#is_group) is true, even over a set photo
- the [`profile_picture()`](#profile_picture), clipped to the circle
- [`effective_initials()`](#effective_initials)
- the "Contact" glyph

The badge is an accent-filled circle in the top-right corner, at half the picture's size. It shows a positive [`badge_number()`](#badge_number), as "99+" past 99, or else the [`badge_icon()`](#badge_icon). Screen readers hear the person's name followed by ", N items", ", icon" or [`badge_text()`](#badge_text). The name is "Group", the display name, the initials or "Person". [`ui::PersonPicture`](#uipersonpicture) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 12,
    .content  = {
        ui::PersonPicture{.display_name = "Jane Doe"},  // shows "JD"
        ui::PersonPicture{.display_name = "Jane Doe", .badge_number = 5, .width = 72.0f},
        ui::PersonPicture{.group        = true},              // the People glyph
    },
});

// Imperatively:
auto avatar = std::make_unique<ui::PersonPictureControl>();
avatar->set_display_name("Alex Wilber");
avatar->set_diameter(48.0f);
avatar->set_badge_number(3);
avatar->set_badge_text("3 unread messages"); // spoken instead of ", 3 items"
```

## `ui::PersonPicture`

A circular avatar with an optional number, glyph or picture badge. It shows a photo, initials or a placeholder glyph, picked in the order [ui::PersonPictureControl](#uipersonpicturecontrol) describes. Builds a [ui::PersonPictureControl](#uipersonpicturecontrol).

The pictures can be bound like every other field. A [Binding](../core/binding.md) doesn't compare its values, only a [Property](../core/property.md) does, so bind a picture through a conversion from another property: [`bind(choice, [](int i) { ... })`](../core/namespace-ui.md#bind).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<int> unread{3};

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 12, .content = {
    ui::PersonPicture{.display_name    = "Jane Doe"}, // shows "JD"
    ui::PersonPicture{.diameter        = 48.0f,
                      .display_name    = "Alex Wilber",
                      .profile_picture = ui::Bitmap::read("alex.png"),
                      .badge_number    = unread,
                      .badge_text      = ui::bind(unread, [](int n) { return std::format("{} unread", n); })},
    ui::PersonPicture{.group           = true},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::PersonPicture{
    .diameter, .display_name, .initials, .group, .profile_picture, .badge_number, .badge_icon,
    .badge_text, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-diameter"></span>`diameter` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{96.0f}` | The circle's diameter in DIPs, at least 1. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-display_name"></span>`display_name` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The person's name. Read by screen readers, and the source of the initials when [`initials`](#uipersonpicture-initials) is empty. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-initials"></span>`initials` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | Initials to show in place of ones derived from [`display_name`](#uipersonpicture-display_name). |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-group"></span>`group` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{false}` | Shows the "People" glyph, over every picture and initial. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-profile_picture"></span>`profile_picture` | `ui::Binding<ui::Bitmap>` |  | The photo, clipped to the circle. Shown in place of the initials. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-badge_number"></span>`badge_number` | `ui::Binding<int>` | `{0}` | The badge number, shown when positive, as "99+" past 99. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-badge_icon"></span>`badge_icon` | `ui::Binding<ui::IconSource>` |  | The badge icon, shown when the number isn't: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph, a path or a picture. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-badge_text"></span>`badge_text` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | What screen readers hear in place of the default ", N items" or ", icon". |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uipersonpicture-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::PersonPicture>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

A circular avatar showing a photo, initials or a placeholder glyph, with an optional badge. It takes no input and never receives focus.

What it shows, in priority order:

### PersonPictureControl

```cpp
PersonPictureControl() = default
```

A 96 DIP placeholder avatar (the "Contact" glyph) with no badge.

### diameter

```cpp
float diameter() const
```

The size when no width or height is set, in DIPs. 96 by default.

### set_diameter

```cpp
void set_diameter(float diameter)
```

Sets the diameter, at least 1 DIP. Updates layout and redraws.

### effective_diameter

```cpp
float effective_diameter() const
```

The size the picture is drawn at. It is [`diameter()`](#diameter) until an explicit width or height is set, then that one, or the smaller when both are, so the picture stays round.


The person's name. The initials and the accessible name are derived from it.


Explicit initials. When not empty, they replace the initials derived from [display_name()](#display_name) (see [`effective_initials()`](#effective_initials)).

### set_initials

```cpp
void set_initials(std::string initials)
```

Sets the explicit initials. Redraws.

### is_group

```cpp
bool is_group() const
```

Whether the picture shows the "People" glyph, even over a set profile picture.

### set_group

```cpp
void set_group(bool group)
```

Turns the group glyph on or off. Redraws.

### profile_picture

```cpp
const Bitmap& profile_picture() const
```

A decoded photo, drawn clipped to the circle. An empty [Bitmap](../rendering/bitmap.md), the default, falls back to the initials.

### set_profile_picture

```cpp

```

Sets the photo. Redraws.

### badge_number

```cpp
int badge_number() const
```

The badge number. 0 or less shows no number.

### set_badge_number

```cpp
void set_badge_number(int number)
```

Sets the badge number. Measures and redraws, since the badge widens for "99+".

### badge_icon

```cpp
const IconSource& badge_icon() const
```

The badge icon, shown while [badge_number()](#badge_number) isn't: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph, a path or a picture. It is drawn at 60% of the badge's size in the badge's text color, and a picture keeps its own colors. Empty shows no icon.

### set_badge_icon

```cpp
void set_badge_icon(IconSource icon)
```

Sets the badge icon. Redraws.

### badge_text

```cpp
const std::string& badge_text() const
```

What screen readers hear in place of ", N items" or ", icon".

### set_badge_text

```cpp
void set_badge_text(std::string text)
```

Sets the badge text. It changes only the accessible name, so nothing is redrawn.

### badge_content

```cpp
std::string badge_content() const
```

The number the badge shows, "99+" past 99. Empty when it shows the icon or nothing.

### has_badge

```cpp
bool has_badge() const
```

Whether any badge shows.

### badge_bounds

```cpp
Rect badge_bounds() const
```

Where the badge is drawn for the current bounds: in the top-right corner, half the picture's size tall, moved 4 DIPs up and right. A circle, widened to the left into a pill when the number doesn't fit in one.

### effective_initials

```cpp
std::string effective_initials() const
```

[initials()](#initials) if set, else initials_from_display_name(display_name()).

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Exposed to UI Automation as text.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

"Group", else the display name, else the initials, else "Person", followed by ", N items", ", icon" or [`badge_text()`](#badge_text) for a badge.

### initials_from_display_name

```cpp
static std::string initials_from_display_name(std::string_view display_name)
```

The initials for [`display_name`](#display_name). For a name in Latin, Cyrillic or a similar script, these are the first characters of the first and last words, upper-cased. A single word gives one initial. A trailing (…), […] or {…} is dropped first, leading punctuation is skipped and combining marks stay with their letter. A name that starts in a script where initials mean nothing, such as CJK, Arabic, Indic or Thai, gives none.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

A square of [`effective_diameter()`](#effective_diameter), clipped to `available` on a bounded axis.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the circle with its photo, initials or glyph, then the badge.
